label: Second copy step (first token fed back) in long sequences, gated on first-token identity (3/h/x/l)
explanation: Very sparse feature (about 0.013% of steps). 78% of activation mass is at recall_idx==1, the step right after <DEL> where the model is fed back original token 0 and outputs token 1. It is concentrated in L=8-9 (t=9,10) and on first tokens 3 and h, with x and l next. The remaining ~22% is in the early original phase (t=2-4), mostly right after an s at t-1 or t-2 (e.g. s s [v]). Never fires at t<2, at the delimiter, or at copy steps after recall_idx 1. Activations are uniformly small (max 0.24) and coverage is flat across activation quartiles, so no checked magnitude modulator was found. Precision is very poor even for the best conjunction: most matching contexts stay silent, so firing depends on finer sequence content that no simple predicate captured.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues. Raise it: phase=2 & in_tok=3 (+4.56), orig1=s (+4.51), recall_idx=1 (+3.77), prev_tok=<DEL> (+3.77), orig2=s (+3.44), orig0=s (+3.09). Lower it: out_tok=s (-4.61), correct=1 (-4.60), in_tok=s (-3.68), orig_idx=-1 (-3.12).
